macros.name: annotate
macros.doc: \annotate{x}{y}{text} Puts the text, between dollars, in a zero width box at offset (x, y) modules from the position of the \annotate command (which is generally the first command(s) after entering math-mode).

macros.name: belowl
macros.doc: \belowl{} A common pattern in diagrams is to have a pair of incoming or outgoing propagators. If the lower one of this pair is enclosed within \belowl{...}, then it is set so that it occupies zero horizontal space, and moved leftwards and downwards, to fit under the upper of the pair of propagators.

macros.name: Diagram
macros.doc: \Diagram{} This is for building more complicated diagrams. It takes one argument, which is like the contents of an {array} environment—a series of formulae separated by &’s and \\.

macros.name: feyn
macros.doc: \feyn Selects the diagram font, in display style – that is, suitable for a displayed equation.

macros.name: feynstrut
macros.doc: \feynstrut{h}{d} For use within an (eqn)array environment, or the like. It modifies the control sequence \strut to be a strut of height h and depth d modules, which can therefore be used to space the array out.

macros.name: maxis
macros.doc: \maxis Raises a formula to the math-axis, which is occasionally useful within intext equations: eg $\Feyn{fglf} - \maxis{\Feyn{faf}}$ produces fyf − faf.

macros.name: momentum
macros.doc: \momentum{ch}{text} sets the character ‘ch’, which may be a ligature, and puts the given text at the recommended annotation position for that character.

macros.name: vertexlabel
macros.doc: \vertexlabel{p}{text} Allows you to label a vertex.
